evals.prompt: Draft a new page about configuring Fleet server TLS. Audience: operators with Elastic Stack experience. Purpose: walk through generating certs and applying them to Fleet server. Stack 9.0+, no serverless.
evals.expected_output: A how-to page with frontmatter (type: how-to, applies_to stack: ga 9.0+, serverless: unavailable), action-verb H1, Before you begin section, numbered steps, and a Related section.
expectations: Classifies as how-to (not overview) because task is procedural
Frontmatter includes type: how-to
applies_to sets serverless: unavailable because Fleet Server is Stack-only
H1 uses action-verb pattern: 'Configure Fleet server TLS'
Includes a Before you begin section listing cert prerequisites
Steps are numbered, each step contains one instruction
Related section links to Fleet enrollment, TLS reference, or similar pages
Reading test subagent is invoked and its report is presented

evals.prompt: I want to write a page explaining what ES|QL is for a developer who has never used it. No issue, no target path yet.
evals.expected_output: Skill asks intake questions (audience, purpose, context, target location), classifies as overview, searches related docs, drafts with applies_to for both stack and serverless, runs reading test.
expectations: Uses AskUserQuestion to gather audience, purpose, context, and target location before drafting
Classifies as overview (not how-to) because topic is conceptual
Frontmatter includes type: overview
applies_to covers both stack and serverless (ES|QL is available on both)
Searches Elastic docs MCP for existing ES|QL pages and reports duplication risk
Draft includes what ES|QL is, how it works, and why it matters
Related section links to ES|QL tutorials, how-tos, and reference pages
Reading test report flags any jargon that would confuse a new developer

evals.prompt: Draft a troubleshooting page for the error 'index_not_found_exception' in Elasticsearch. Audience: developers. Stack and serverless.
evals.expected_output: A troubleshooting page with a Symptoms section, a Resolution section, applies_to for both stack and serverless, and a problem-focused H1.
expectations: Classifies as troubleshooting
H1 is problem-focused: 'index_not_found_exception errors' or similar
Includes Symptoms section with exact error message in monospace
Includes Resolution section with steps ordered most-common-fix first
Frontmatter type: troubleshooting
applies_to covers stack and serverless
Does not include a long conceptual explanation before the fix
Reading test subagent checks whether a reader in production crisis can find the fix quickly

evals.prompt: There is already a page about Kibana alerting at https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/alerts-cases/alerts. I want to add a new page about alert suppression. Should I create a new page or extend the existing one?
evals.expected_output: Skill checks docs coherence for alerting suppression, surfaces the existing alerts page, and surfaces the question to the user before drafting.
expectations: Uses elastic-docs MCP search_docs or find_related_docs to discover existing alert suppression content
Surfaces any existing alert suppression coverage to the user
Asks the user whether to create a new page or extend the existing one before drafting
Does not draft without user confirmation when duplication risk is present

evals.prompt: I have a GitHub issue at elastic/docs-content#9999 that asks to document the new --reindex-on-startup CLI flag for Elasticsearch. The feature ships in 9.5.
evals.expected_output: Skill fetches the issue, classifies the page as a how-to or reference, sets applies_to stack: ga 9.5+, serverless: unavailable (CLI flag is Stack-only), drafts the page, and runs the reading test.
expectations: Runs gh issue view 9999 --repo elastic/docs-content
Extracts scope, audience, and applies_to hints from the issue
Classifies as how-to (procedural flag usage) or reference
applies_to sets stack: ga 9.5+
applies_to sets serverless: unavailable because CLI flags are Stack-only
Draft includes the flag name in monospace, its purpose, and a usage example
Reading test subagent is invoked with the classified audience from the issue
